justifications.clinical.clinicalOutcomes: Enables upright mobility and stepping in complete SCI; for ambulatory patients with partial injury, not superior to conventional.
justifications.clinical.efficiency: Device-specific manufacturer training; requires institutional access to exoskeleton system.
justifications.clinical.caseloadApplicability: Extremely limited by equipment access and patient eligibility; applicable mainly in research or SCI/stroke centers.
justifications.clinical.reimbursement: Very limited insurance coverage; some workers comp and select commercial beginning to cover; primarily research or cash-pay settings.
justifications.clinical.marketDemand: Growing interest but very limited current employer demand; primarily research hospitals and specialized centers.
justifications.clinical.patientSatisfaction: High psychological value of upright posture for wheelchair users; fatigue and safety concerns limit enthusiasm.
justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Ekso, ReWalk, Indego, and Wandercraft hire clinical specialists and trainers.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Small vendor pool but each has dedicated clinical-specialist roles.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Moderate premium for device-specialist roles at robotics vendors.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Builds genuine familiarity with robotic gait device mechanics and patient programming.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Direct bridge into medical-robotics industry roles.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: High training investment relative to small vendor market.
justifications.business.cashPayViability: SCI/stroke families pay cash for gait time; market is small but motivated.
justifications.business.pricingLeverage: Novelty and capital cost support premium per-session pricing.
justifications.business.marketDifferentiation: Very few clinics own exoskeletons — strong differentiation.
justifications.business.ownerLeverage: Equipment-driven; staff can be trained, though caseload is limited.
justifications.business.marketDemand: Niche neuro population; broader consumer demand is modest.
justifications.business.efficiency: Vendor training is short, but device cost ($75-150K) is prohibitive.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyRecognition: Valued in neuro rehab research labs; not a standalone promotion criterion.
justifications.academicClinical.scholarship: Growing literature in SCI and stroke gait recovery.
justifications.academicClinical.teachingValue: Useful for neuro rehab and rehab technology coursework.
justifications.academicClinical.evidenceDepth: Mixed — improvements documented but long-term functional gains debated.
justifications.academicClinical.facultyDemand: Rarely a posting requirement; relevant to research-active programs.
justifications.academicClinical.efficiency: Training is fast, but academic payoff depends on institutional equipment access.
